title: impl-result schema rejected by real codex structured outputs (invalid_json_schema)
description: First real impl-lane spawn (worker impl-0824t1849-lipo, 2026-08-24) died at turn end: API error invalid_request_error/invalid_json_schema — "In context=('properties','evidence'), 'additionalProperties' is required to be supplied and to be false." The shipped templates/impl-result.schema.json deliberately sets evidence additionalProperties:true (P4 Task 9 pin) — valid JSON Schema, invalid for OpenAI strict structured outputs, and the real --output-schema acceptance was a recorded deferred follow-up. Fix: make the template strict-valid (evidence additionalProperties:false + required [logs_excerpts]; drop the four documented-optional subkeys or require them), update the P4 pin tests (spawn.rs/templates.rs schema unit tests; repo schema_gate only checks top-level required so fixtures stay green), re-verify with one real impl spawn. Workaround in use meanwhile: explicit --schema /tmp/devloop-run-mesh/impl-result-strict.schema.json on every devloop dispatch.
notes: Fix in working tree (template + spawn.rs pin test updated; evidence narrowed to required [logs_excerpts], closed objects throughout, rationale + live API error recorded in the schema description). title: Agent mesh: any-to-any agent communication, buzz feed, public endpoint registry
description:
Expand a2a beyond claude→codex dispatch into a full agent mesh, in two layers.

LAYER 1 — internal any-to-any: every local agent (claude sessions, codex workers) can discover each other, announce what it is working on, and push relevant context to another agent. Directions: claude↔claude, codex↔codex, codex→claude (claude→codex already exists via a2a spawn/send). Likely rides the existing a2a broker + file layer (owner registry, outbox/inbox) — brainstorm first.

LAYER 2 — 'slack for agents' (buzz-style, API-level): agents publish status/updates to a feed other agents subscribe to; direct fill-ins between agents over an agent-to-agent protocol. Transport: whatever is most efficient (HTTP/WebSocket first candidates; TCP/UDP if warranted). Public exposure via ngrok (or similar) hole-punch. Discovery via a public agent endpoint registry — centralized or decentralized; candidate backends: redis cluster or Neon postgres. Registry records per endpoint: owner, endpoint URL, created_at, actively-working flag, staleness since last update.

Workflow: superpowers:brainstorming first, then spec, then devloop plans — same lifecycle as a2a phases 1-5. Origin: Mike, 2026-08-20.
